content:
Ommatidia are the repeating structural units found in the compound eyes of arthropods such as crustaceans and insects. Each ommatidium functions as a separate photoreceptor, and together they form a mosaic image. Eyespots are simple light-sensitive structures found in some invertebrates, simple eyes (ocelli) have a single lens, and binocular vision refers to the overlapping visual fields of two eyes, not a structural unit like ommatidia.
